title: Review of the Marangoni turnover-tuning negative on fresh seed 81: returning the removed matter (REDIST) again beats plain dilution (24 vs 16 persistent splits, generation 6 vs 3), but on this seed plain p 0.10 still divides in frames 100-140, so the 'stops after frame 120' part does not replicate cleanly
summary: The finding's world.py, 128^2, 150 frames, seed 81, labkit; c00's extract.py and the finding's turnover_stats.py unchanged. p_dil 0.10: 16 bodies removed in 15 events, 16 persistent splits, generation 3; splits per 20 frames 0, 4, 4, 0, 1, 5, 2, 0; bodies 7 -> 25 (still rising at the end; sheet.png shows the box filling slowly from 2 early nucleations); 6 dividing tracks, none >= 3 rod lengths. p_dil 0.10 with REDIST: 18 removed, 24 persistent splits, generation 6; splits 0, 4, 5, 3, 1, 8, 3, 0; bodies 28 at the end; 12 dividing tracks, none >= 3 (best 2.66). Both settings have 0 splits in frames 140-150, but the plain-dilution run had not reached the plateau the finding's seed 80 reached, so on this seed it does not show that dilution fails once the population saturates.

observations.D: runs/p010/stats.txt: 16 persistent splits, splits in 100-140 = 7, 0 in 140-150; runs/p010_redist/stats.txt: 24 splits, generation 6

seeds_run.result: partial: REDIST > plain dilution replicates; plain dilution still divides in frames 100-140 because the population fills late on this seed; 0 of 18 dividing tracks >= 3 rod lengths

controls_run.D: runs/p010_redist (same seed, removed matter returned at once)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, two of the eight settings, 150 frames. Seed 81 nucleates only 2 rods early and is still filling at frame 150, so it is not a test of the saturated regime; a longer run (c45's T=2000 follow-up) is the better test.
